title: Learning Through Technology Contact Us
before:
Emma-Marie Banks
Learning Through Technology Coordinator

Emma leads the Learning Through Technology team, guiding operations, long-term planning, and statewide vision. She ensures Maine schools and educators have the resources, training, and tools needed to prepare students with the skills to be “future-ready.” From identifying the most relevant supports for schools to monitoring emerging technology trends, Emma helps align Maine’s educational technology efforts with both state and national priorities. 

Contact Emma for:

  • Program information and statewide initiatives
  • National insights and perspectives on educational technology
  • State-level visioning and planning support
  • Pedagogy, instructional design, and effective technology integration

Email: Emma-Marie.Banks@maine.gov
Phone: 207-816-0280

Bethany Billinger
MLTI Project Manager

Bethany is the core of operational support for the Learning Through Technology team, helping Maine schools access the guidance, resources, and programs needed to integrate technology effectively. She coordinates statewide initiatives like MLTI and the device program, organizes key events including the annual student conferences, oversees grants and contracts, and provides support for communications and program tools. 

Contact Bethany for:

  • Maine Learning Through Technology (MLTI) program information and statewide technology initiatives
  • Device program information and support 
  • Event information, registration, and support, including Student Conference, Maine Winter Classic, and Computer Science Showcase 
  • Grants, contracts, and opt-in agreements

Email: Bethany.Billinger@maine.gov
Phone: 207-816-0278

Allison Braley
Computer Science Specialist

Allison is the go-to for all things computer science education. From developing resources and curriculum to organizing statewide programs and events, she supports schools, educators, and districts in building high-quality computer science opportunities for all students. She leads initiatives like the Statewide Computer Science Leadership Team, Pine Tree Programming and Dirigo Digital, provides professional learning for teachers, and collaborates with state and national partners to align policy and practice. 

Contact Allison for:

  • Computer science curriculum guidance, resources, and professional development opportunities
  • Information on statewide CS programs, events, and initiatives (Pine Tree Programming, CS Showcase, Dirigo Digital)
  • Support for integrating computer science and digital literacy across grade levels and content areas

Email: Allison.Braley@maine.gov
Phone: 207-215-6463

 

Jim Chasse
Infrastructure Specialist

Jim is the primary contact for cyber infrastructure, cybersecurity, and state and federal resources that strengthen local technology systems. He also serves as a key point of contact for the Student Data Privacy Consortium. From guiding network infrastructure improvements in schools to helping districts enhance their cybersecurity posture, Jim provides statewide leadership and expertise to ensure Maine’s schools are secure, connected, and future-ready. 

Contact Jim for:

  • Support with school technology infrastructure and connectivity
  • Guidance on funding and capacity-building for infrastructure improvements
  • Expertise in statewide network, cybersecurity, and technical support
  • Assistance with the K–12 State and Local Cybersecurity Grant
  • Presentations on cybersecurity, safety, and infrastructure best practices
  • Participation in the annual K–12 CyberStorm! tabletop exercise

Email: James.Chasse@maine.gov
Phone: 207-707-0486

Nicole Davis
Emerging Technology Specialist

Nicole is the Learning Through Technology Teams Emerging and AI expert and focuses on supporting emerging technologies in education. From answering questions to implementing AI, she empowers educators to navigate and integrate emerging technologies with confidence and purpose.

Contact Nicole for:

  • Support with AI and Emerging Technology
  • Professional Learning Solutions
  • Statewide Guidance and Resources

Email: nicole.davis@maine.gov
Phone: (207) 816-1708

Jon Graham
Elementary Technology Specialist

Jon supports all things elementary technology and the Learning Through Technology’s student leadership programming. From helping to facilitate our annual student events to supporting technology integration in the elementary classroom and bringing new opportunities into libraries and media centers, Jon works to help educators connect with the education technology opportunities best suited for them and their students. 

Contact Jon for:

  • Questions related to elementary level (PK-8) technology integration and use
  • Participation in Student Leadership events (MLTI Student Conference, Maine Winter Classic and SLAM)
  • Opportunities to present or showcase at our events (MLTI Student Conference, CS Ed Showcase)

Email: Jonathan.M.Graham@maine.gov
Phone: 207-441-0674

 

Sam Jenkins
Education Data Specialist

Sam is the Learning Through Technology’s go-to data guru. From collecting, organizing, and cleaning data to analyzing and visualizing it, he not only works with data but supports other initiatives on the team as well, like events and contracts.

Contact Sam for:

  • Device program information and support.
  • Event registration and support for the Student Conference and Maine Winter Classic.
  • MLTI Opt-in agreement submissions and questions.
  • Updating contacts for mailing lists and general correspondence.

Email: Samuel.Jenkins@maine.gov
Phone: 207-458-9891

Haley Neal
Office Specialist

Haley is the procurement and administrative go-to on the Learning Through Technology team, providing support with grants, contracts, invoicing, vendor coordination, and process guidance to ensure smooth operations. 

Contact Haley for:

  • Invoicing inquiries and support
  • Contract-related questions and support
  • Vendor Code or Vendor Portal inquiries and support

Email: Haley.Neal@maine.gov
Phone: 207-707-0485

Jonathan R. Werner, M.S.Ed.
MLTI Ambassador Program Facilitator

Jonathan oversees the MLTI Ambassador program and helps to coordinate the Learning Through Technology team’s professional learning offerings at-large. His work is always motived by his passion for shifting from simply having technology in schools to using educational technology in ways that transform students’ experiences and learning.

Contact Jonathan for:

  • Questions related to Digital Citizenship and Digital Leadership
  • Inquiries regarding LTT’s Professional Learning offerings and the team’s support for technology integration statewide
  • Any explorations of technology use in School Libraries, Makerspaces, and Special Education programming.

Email: Jonathan.Werner@maine.gov
Phone: 207-530-2587

notes: 867 words with no section headers at all — the biggest single improvement available here.

decisions.label: Write the email addresses the same way
decisions.why: 2 addresses are shown in whatever case it was typed in. The house form capitalises each name and leaves a middle initial in lower case — nicole.davis@maine.gov → Nicole.Davis@maine.gov. Only the first letter of each part changes, so a name that spells itself LaBreck keeps doing so.

decisions.label: Put the card titles on one level
decisions.why: 18 card titles are written at a level copied from an example rather than chosen — h5 on a page whose sections are h2. Only the number changes.

decisions.label: Make a loose address look like an address
decisions.why: 9 email addresses sit in the body of this page rather than in a contact block, drawn exactly like every other link — so the one that opens a mail window looks the same as the ones that go to web pages. The chip carries the same envelope the banner's contact link uses. The address itself does not change.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.

decisions.label: Let a portrait photograph keep its shape
decisions.why: 9 card pictures are taller than they are wide — headshots, mostly — and every card image is cropped to 16:9, so most of the person is thrown away to make a landscape strip. Measured from the files: these are 500x667 rendered into 293x165. Marked as portrait, the card gives them a shape they fit and the picture runs up the card instead. The file does not change.

decisions.label: One title bar to a card, not two
decisions.why: 9 cards open with two headings of the same rank one above the other — the person's name and then their job title — so the card has two identical title bars and a screen reader announces two headings where one thing is being named. The job title becomes the subtitle it already reads as. The words do not change.
